worst_samples.question: To what waters do the COLREGs apply?
worst_samples.gold_answer: To all vessels upon the high seas and in all waters connected therewith navigable by seagoing vessels.
worst_samples.answer: The COLREGs (International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea) apply to all sea areas except where specifically excluded by paragraph 3 of Article III of the Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972. worst_samples.question: Can local authorities make special rules for roadsteads, harbours, rivers, lakes or inland waterways?
worst_samples.gold_answer: Yes, provided they conform as closely as possible to the international Rules.
worst_samples.answer: Yes, local authorities can make special rules for roadsteads, harbours, rivers, lakes, or inland waterways as long as these rules do not conflict with the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs) or other international conventions.
